title: The red-team that attacked production
blurb: The draft resolved an arbitrary URL and probes hit production.
prompt: A red-team run accidentally sent adversarial probes to production, because the draft accepted any target URL and never enforced the non-production registry. The same draft re-ran probes on retry and skipped coverage silently. Review it, fix it, and prove targets are registered and coverage is honest.
aiNote: The draft accepts an arbitrary URL as a target with no registry check, so a typo in the target field points the entire probe set at production, and its probe dedupe is a non-atomic check-then-set that re-executes concurrent probes.
testIdea: Submit a production URL and assert 400 before any probe is sent; fire the kill switch mid-run and assert every runner stops before its next probe; assert a run with skipped categories never reports pass.
followUps: How would you scope a probe category before it runs?
What evidence bundle should a finding carry to be reproducible?
When should a kill switch require a human to reset?
